newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -NYMEX crude led by gasoline above 60 cts.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -NYMEX crude led by gasoline above 60 cts.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+NYMEX crude is relatively bullish but is riding on the coat tails of gasoline which broke above the key 60 cents level on Wednesday. This number remains a key barometer for energy markets.
NYMEX crude oil futures are more likely than not to test higher on Thursday but much depends on the performance of gasoline, traders and technical analysts said.
"I am modestly bullish," said Victor Yu at Refco in New York. "But a lot lies on the shoulders of gasoline. "We got convincingly over 60 cents yesterday and that is an important number."
August WTI crude oil closed two cents a barrel lower on Wednesday at $19.65 while August gasoline ended the day 0.52 cents a gallon up at 60.46 cents.
August heating oil, meanwhile, was 0.27 cents a gallon weaker at 52.68.

Gasoline, Yu said, would find support in the short term at 60 cents and then at 59.50 below that. A little resistance would appear at 60.70 cents, the high point reached on Wednesday's chart. "If we get through there we could see another couple of cents on gasoline.
He said that an important number on the upside for crude would be $20.05, which represents the 38 percent Fibonacci retracement from the 22.30 high on May 16 to the $18.65 low of June 20.

On the downside, he suggested that the pivot point (mid range of yesterday's trade) lay at around $19.65, which was also the price at the close of business on Wedesday. This could provide a little support to a stronger market.
Below that, Yu saw $19.50 as support. The expiry of crude options would add volatility to the mix, he said, and this could lead to a test of either support or resistance.

Charles Gray at Prudential-bache futures in London said: "The option expiry today for August WTI implies, in a quiet market, that WTI will gravitate towards a strike price - the most nearby being $19.50.
"The anemic nature of market strength implies we need a catalyst to enable a breakout."
He suggested that the best chance of this came from gasoline, which has broken above a flag formation, implying a potential move up to 63.00 cents.
